THE E7 REVERSAL COST TWO CYCLES AND IS THE ONE TO REMEMBER. Cycle 2 added resolved_to but in a different field ORDER than the parent SPEC.md. CYCLE 2 INVERTED FR-011's GATE AND CYCLE 3 CAUGHT IT. As written after cycle 2, FR-011 read as though the 4.9.0 RELEASE were the gate permitting assistant-side work. The gate is D4's EVIDENCE requirement -- 'Part A proven', not 'Part A released'. That distinction IS the CP2a/CP2a-bridge seam; collapsing it recreates the posture D-00 exists to prevent. Now separated at spec.md:255-261.

FR-043 IS PARTIALLY REFUTED BY LCM REALITY (spurt 1's most valuable finding, now fully absorbed into the spec). HCParser.Update() is itself conditional -- 'if (m_changeListener.Reset() || m_forceUpdate) LoadParser();' -- so Reload()->Update() as originally specced does NOT unconditionally discard. FieldWorks' own force-reload path is ParserWorker.ReloadGrammarAndLexicon(): Reset() THEN update. Bound wrong, it fails SILENTLY and serves the next parse from the stale grammar the caller believes it discarded.

Reset() and IsUpToDate() are MISSING from parser_probe.py's HCPARSER_MEMBERS, but FR-041/SC-016 forbid touching that file. Resolved by D-02: each check probes what its own surface binds -- the requirement lands on the NEW flexicon-side probe, parser_probe.py stays untouched, SC-016 stays green. The two member lists diverge in BOTH directions after CP2, which the spec now says (E3).

THERE IS NO JOB/QUEUE/WORKER/RUN-RECORD MACHINERY ANYWHERE in this repo. SessionState is in-memory; run_script_async is one create_subprocess_exec + wait_for with no handle and no cancellation token; the only concurrency primitive on the request path is kernel.project_write_locks (per-project asyncio.Lock). US4 extends NOTHING -- 100% net-new. Best structural precedent for the run record is skeleton_storage.py:43-50 (JSONL append under a threading.Lock + env dir override).

The flexicon_lcm_bridge_v<ver>.json sibling is version-locked to the flexicon version (server.py:665 loads it keyed to self.flexicon_version, handlers/equivalence.py:64 consumes it). refresh.py:217 derives the bridge prefix, so a FULL refresh produces both files; the risk is a hand-copied index. The spec now names both artifacts explicitly (E1).

FR-010 identity holds at OBJECT level only for ParseWord (MorphInfo carries real IMoForm/IMoMorphSynAnalysis refs). ParseWordXml/TraceWordXml return an already-serialized XDocument where objects are Hvo integer attributes only. Do NOT plan a typed object-identity marshaller for the trace.

Allomorph->owning-entry is a flexicon WRAPPER gap, not an LCM gap -- MoForm.OwningEntry already exists (OverridesLing_MoClasses.cs:3113) and four sibling GetOwningEntry templates exist in flexicon. Scopes that deliverable down to ~20 lines. Genres and MSA reads are real gaps; MSA is the nontrivial one (subtypes expose different property sets, so it is not one flat wrapper).

FR-017's no-XCore guarantee rests on .NET LAZY PER-TYPE BINDING, not on absence of a reference: ParserCore.csproj DOES reference xCore/xCoreInterfaces/FwUtils at assembly level; the 'using XCore;' statements are confined to ParseFiler/ParserScheduler/ParserWorker, not HCParser/HCLoader/IParser.
